quizzes.title: EU Associate Membership Proposal
quizzes.passage:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed exploring a new form of relationship that could enable Canada to become an 'Associate Member' of the European Union. The proposal is linked to an 'Alliance for the Future', which would promote greater cooperation between Europe and Canada in areas such as defence, critical supply chains, technology, clean energy, strategic industries and Arctic security. The idea is presented as a possible new model of engagement between the EU and a non-EU country.

Under such an arrangement, Canada could participate more closely in selected European frameworks without becoming a full member. Participation could cover selected EU programmes, cooperation in defence procurement and collaboration in emerging technologies. However, it would not automatically provide EU institutional membership, voting rights, representation in the European Parliament or automatic access to the Single Market.

The term 'Associate Member' is not an established membership category under the EU's foundational treaties. One route would be formal treaty revision, which would require the relevant EU treaties to be amended. A more flexible alternative is a sui generis arrangement, meaning a specially designed relationship tailored to the circumstances of the EU and its partner. Such an arrangement could establish special economic cooperation, institutional dialogue and sector-specific integration without formally creating a new category of EU membership.

questions.q: Which article of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union is cited for negotiating a special Association Agreement?
questions.explanation: The booklet cites Article 217 of the TFEU as the basis for negotiating a special Association Agreement.

questions.q: Which EU bodies must give approval for an Association Agreement?
options: Unanimous approval in the Council and consent of the European Parliament
Approval by the European Commission alone
Qualified majority approval in the European Council only
Ratification by the national parliaments of all member states
questions.explanation: An Association Agreement needs unanimous approval in the Council of the EU and the consent of the European Parliament.

questions.q: In which city did 128 countries reach a consensus on a working definition of Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems under the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons?
questions.explanation: The consensus was reached in Geneva under the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Formal treaty revision is a route that is hard to achieve for creating a new category of EU membership.
Reason (R): All 27 EU Member States would have to agree to a treaty revision.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Treaty revision is hard because all 27 Member States must agree, which is why R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Vienna Convention   ->   A. 2016
II. Montreal Protocol   ->   B. 1973
III. Kigali Amendment   ->   C. 1985
IV. CITES   ->   D. 1987
questions.explanation: The Vienna Convention dates to 1985, the Montreal Protocol to 1987, the Kigali Amendment to 2016, and CITES was signed in 1973.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The CCW was adopted in 1980 and entered into force in 1983.
II. An Association Agreement needs approval only by the European Commission.
III. Treaty revision would require ratification according to the constitutional procedures of individual Member States.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because an Association Agreement needs Council unanimity and Parliament's consent.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Montreal Protocol led to a 99% phase-out of controlled ozone-depleting substances.
II. CITES species are listed in three appendices by conservation status and trade sensitivity.
III. The Kigali Amendment mandates the phase-out of hydrofluorocarbons.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because the Kigali Amendment mandates a phase-down, not a phase-out.

quizzes.title: Arms Control and Wildlife Trade Treaties
quizzes.passage:
The UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons is an arms-control framework that aims to restrict or prohibit weapons considered to have particularly harmful or indiscriminate effects. Countries meeting in Geneva recently reached a working definition of lethal autonomous weapons systems, commonly called killer robots. Such systems can identify and attack targets with limited or no meaningful human intervention. The Convention is commonly known as the Inhumane Weapons Convention, and India is a State Party to it.

The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, known as CITES, regulates international trade in endangered wild species. It is legally binding but does not override national laws, and its Conferences of the Parties review its decisions every two to three years. Its Secretariat functions under the UN Environment Programme. Parties appoint authorities for permits and scientific advice, and CITES species are listed by conservation status and trade sensitivity. India is among its members.

Ozone protection is governed by a separate set of agreements. The Vienna Convention was the first global treaty recognising ozone depletion. A landmark later agreement led to a near-complete phase-out of controlled ozone-depleting substances. The Kigali Amendment, adopted in 2016, followed as a further step in this framework.

questions.q: How many countries reached a consensus on a working definition of lethal autonomous weapons systems under the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons?
questions.explanation: The booklet reports that 128 countries reached this consensus in Geneva.

questions.q: In which year was the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons adopted?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 1980 as the year the Convention was adopted, and it entered into force in 1983.

questions.q: In which year was the Vienna Convention adopted?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Vienna Convention as 1985, the first global treaty recognising ozone depletion.

questions.q: In which year was the Montreal Protocol adopted?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Montreal Protocol to 1987, when it led to a 99% phase-out of controlled ozone-depleting substances.

questions.q: The Kigali Amendment (2016) mandates the phase-down of which group of chemicals?
questions.explanation: The Kigali Amendment mandates the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons, commonly called HFCs.

questions.q: In which year did India become a Party to CITES?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India became a Party to CITES in 1976.

questions.q: In which US city was CITES formally signed?
questions.explanation: The booklet says CITES was formally signed in 1973 in Washington, D.C.

quizzes.title: Political Funding, Time Standard and Schemes
quizzes.passage:
The PM Vishwakarma scheme completed three years of implementation in September 2026. It supports traditional artisans with a focus on district saturation, brand promotion and market linkages. The scheme covers 18 traditional trades in rural and urban areas, and its benefits are meant for artisans in the unorganised sector. Beneficiaries receive an ID card, and the scheme offers basic and advanced training.

Concerns over political funding transparency have intensified amid allegations involving registered unrecognised political parties. A political party can apply to the Election Commission of India for registration under the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Registered parties must maintain records of specified contributions, file annual contribution reports and comply with audit and tax requirements. The Election Commission maintains and publishes information on registered, delisted and disputed parties, and such parties may receive certain electoral benefits.

The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 have been notified by the Department of Consumer Affairs. They make Indian Standard Time the single mandatory time reference for legal, administrative, commercial and official purposes across India. The rules are part of the 'One Nation, One Time' initiative, promote the use of NavIC and will come into force 180 days after their publication in the Official Gazette.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution does the superintendence, direction and control of elections vest in the Election Commission of India?
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.

questions.q: Under Section 52 of which Act were the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 notified?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the IST Rules were notified under Section 52 of the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.

questions.q: Which institution is the custodian of India's national time standard?
questions.explanation: The booklet names CSIR-National Physical Laboratory in New Delhi as the custodian of India's national time standard.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Registered Unrecognised Political Parties have come under scrutiny over political funding transparency.
Reason (R): They are registered with the Election Commission of India but have not acquired the status of a recognised State or National Party.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but R only defines RUPPs and does not explain why they face scrutiny.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Section 29A of RPA, 1951   ->   C. Contribution reports
II. Section 29B of RPA, 1951   ->   A. Tax exemptions for eligible parties
III. Section 29C of RPA, 1951   ->   D. Voluntary contributions from individuals and companies
IV. Section 13A of Income Tax Act, 1961   ->   B. Registration of political parties
questions.explanation: Section 29A covers registration, 29B voluntary contributions, 29C contribution reports, and Section 13A tax exemptions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian Standard Time:
I. IST is based on 82.5 degrees East longitude.
II. IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Coordinated Universal Time.
III. The Standard Meridian of IST passes through Tamil Nadu.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because the Standard Meridian passes through Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The PM Vishwakarma scheme is fully funded by the Government of India.
II. Only one member per family can apply for the scheme's benefits.
III. Applicants who benefited from PM Swanidhi in the past five years are eligible to apply.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III is wrong because past beneficiaries of PM Swanidhi in the past five years are not eligible.

quizzes.title: Tulu, Electoral Bonds and Standard Time
quizzes.passage:
The PM Vishwakarma scheme completed three years of implementation in September 2026, supporting traditional artisans with skill training and collateral-free loans.

Tulu is a Dravidian language spoken mainly along India's south-western coast, in the Tulunadu region of Karnataka and parts of Kasaragod district in Kerala. Its script, Tigalari, is a Southern Brahmic script. Before the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, Tulu-speaking coastal areas were associated with the Madras Presidency. They later became part of a unified Mysore State, which was subsequently renamed.

The Karnataka government has now granted Tulu the status of additional administrative language in the state. The decision followed the recommendations of a committee constituted to examine the status of Tulu and Tuluva culture.

In Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India, the Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme. Political parties are registered with the Election Commission under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and registered parties must submit contribution reports.

Indian Standard Time is also being formalised. The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 make IST the single mandatory time reference for official purposes, and the national time standard is maintained using highly precise atomic clocks. The rules also promote the use of NavIC and indigenous timing infrastructure.

questions.q: Up to which financial year does the PM Vishwakarma scheme run?
questions.explanation: The booklet states the scheme runs from FY 2023-24 to FY 2027-28.

questions.q: In which year did the Supreme Court strike down the Electoral Bond Scheme in ADR v. Union of India?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the ADR v. Union of India judgment that struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme to 2024.

questions.q: Under which Section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 are political parties registered with the Election Commission?
questions.explanation: Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides for registration of political parties.

questions.q: In which year was the unified Mysore State renamed Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the unified Mysore State was renamed Karnataka in 1973.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution can a State Legislature adopt Hindi, or one or more languages in use in the State, as its official language?
questions.explanation: Article 345 empowers the State Legislature to adopt such languages.

questions.q: Who headed the committee constituted in 2023 to examine the status of the Tulu language?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the committee was headed by educationist M. Mohan Alva.

questions.q: Which institution is the custodian of India's national time standard?
questions.explanation: The booklet names CSIR-National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi, as the custodian of India's national time standard.

quizzes.title: Space, Orangutans and Film Awards
quizzes.passage:
NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has been launched to study dark energy, dark matter and exoplanets. It is designed to complement the Hubble and James Webb space telescopes and to investigate the structure of galaxies. Its international collaborators include the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.

Five young orangutans were rescued in Odisha and moved to a zoo. Orangutans are arboreal, spending much of their lives in trees, and their natural range is tropical forests.

World Rhino Day is observed on 22 September to raise awareness about the conservation of the world's five remaining rhinoceros species. The day was declared by WWF in 2010. The International Rhino Foundation releases an annual assessment of rhino populations, called the State of Rhino Report, which examines population trends, conservation status and major threats to rhino survival.

The National Film Awards recognise films and cinematic writing. They are announced by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, and the President of India presents the awards at a formal ceremony, traditionally held in New Delhi. The awards cover works produced in different Indian languages and regions, including feature films, non-feature films and writing on cinema, and they honour films from the 2024 calendar year.

questions.q: Which rhinoceros species is the largest of the five and is concentrated in Kaziranga National Park, Assam?
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies the Greater One-Horned Rhino as the largest of the five species, with its major population in Kaziranga.

questions.q: Which national park is home to the last remaining wild Javan rhinos?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Ujung Kulon National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is home to the last remaining wild Javan rhinos.

questions.q: What is the 2026 theme of World Rhino Day?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the 2026 theme of World Rhino Day as 'Keep the Five Alive'.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): International commercial trade in orangutans is prohibited.
Reason (R): Orangutans are covered by CITES, the convention on international trade in endangered wild fauna and flora.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet states that commercial trade in orangutans is prohibited under CITES, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Cosmic Dark Ages   ->   D. Proposed lunar-orbiting satellite
II. PRATUSH   ->   C. Launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy
III. Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope   ->   B. Indigenous radio-astronomy project
IV. CosmoCube   ->   A. Period after CMB formation and before first stars
questions.explanation: The Cosmic Dark Ages match A, PRATUSH matches B, the Roman telescope matches C (Falcon Heavy launch), and CosmoCube matches D.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about orangutans and rhinos:
I. Orangutans are native to India.
II. The word orangutan originates from the Malay language.
III. The Greater One-Horned Rhinoceros is identified by a single black horn.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements II and III are correct, while I is wrong because orangutans are not native to India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope operates near the Sun-Earth L2 point.
II. The National Film Awards were established in 1973.
III. The Directorate of Film Festivals has administered the National Film Awards since 1973.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the National Film Awards were established in 1954.

quizzes.title: Telescopes, Orangutans and Awards
quizzes.passage:
NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has been launched to study dark energy and exoplanets. It is a next-generation flagship observatory designed to complement the Hubble and James Webb space telescopes. The telescope is meant to investigate major questions concerning cosmic expansion and galaxy evolution.

Five young orangutans were rescued in Odisha and later moved to a zoological park. Orangutans are arboreal, spending much of their lives in trees. They are not native to India, and their natural range is restricted to tropical forests of Borneo and Sumatra. International commercial trade in orangutans is prohibited under CITES.

World Rhino Day is observed on 22 September to raise awareness about conservation of the world's five remaining rhinoceros species. The Greater One-Horned Rhino is the largest of these species and is concentrated in Kaziranga National Park. Conservation efforts in India include the National Rhino Conservation Strategy, launched in 2019.

The National Film Awards recognise films and cinematic writing and are announced by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The President of India presents the awards at a formal ceremony. The awards cover works produced in different Indian languages and regions, and the latest awards honour films produced in the 2024 calendar year.

questions.q: In which year were the National Film Awards established?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the National Film Awards were established in 1954.

questions.q: On which rocket was NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Roman telescope was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center.

questions.q: In which city's zoological park were the rescued orangutans moved?
questions.explanation: The booklet states the rescued orangutans were moved to Nandankanan Zoological Park in Bhubaneswar.

questions.q: In which Odisha district were the five young orangutans rescued?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the five young orangutans were rescued in Balasore, Odisha.

questions.q: What is the scientific name of the Bornean orangutan?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Bornean Orangutan as Pongo pygmaeus, with Endangered status.

questions.q: In which Indian state is Kaziranga National Park located?
questions.explanation: The booklet places Kaziranga National Park in Assam, where most of India's Greater One-Horned Rhinos are concentrated.

questions.q: Which Hindi film won the Best Feature Film award in the National Film Awards for films of 2024?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Article 370 in Hindi as the Best Feature Film winner.
